parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key the caller chooses for one changing call, up to 255 characters. The same key with the same input answers what the first call answered instead of acting twice. A key belongs to its caller: another caller's same key is another call.

parameters.name: Catalyst-Unattended
parameters.description: `1` on a call of an API credential when nobody watches its terminal, such as `catalyst <kind> publish --yes`. The call is then not its caller's own confirmation: a call that needs one waits in the caller's Inbox and answers `202` with its run, status `pending_confirmation`. It only ever makes a call stricter; a browser session's call ignores it.

202.description: The call waits for somebody else to approve it. This is its Operation Run; read it again at `Location`.

Unauthenticated.description: `UNAUTHENTICATED`: No credential was presented, or the credential is not valid.

Forbidden.description: `FORBIDDEN`: The caller lacks the scope or the right this operation requires. `details.reason` is `two_factor_setup_required` where the instance requires two-factor sign-in and the person signed in with a password, or the owner of the personal key, has not set it up: every operation but `me.get` is refused until they have.

NotFound.description: `NOT_FOUND`: The resource does not exist, is not visible to the caller, or the instance runs without this operation.

Conflict.description: `CONFLICT`: The request conflicts with the current state of the resource.

RevisionConflict.description: `REVISION_CONFLICT`: An asset the call writes is at another revision than the one the call names, or the name it creates is taken or was deleted. Nothing was written. `details.conflicts` names each such asset, with its current revision and who changed it when for an asset the caller may read.

PreconditionRequired.description: `PRECONDITION_REQUIRED`: The call names no `expectedRevision` for an asset it writes. `details.assets` names each. Send the revision that was read, or `null` to create the asset.

Timeout.description: `TIMEOUT`: The instance did not finish the work in time.

ValidationFailed.description: `VALIDATION_FAILED`: Path, query or body do not match the operation's schema.

RateLimited.description: `RATE_LIMITED`: The caller sent too many requests of this operation's rate class. `details.retryAfterSeconds` and the `Retry-After` header give the seconds to wait. The numbers are the instance's, set under `rateLimits` in its release config.

Internal.description: `INTERNAL`: The instance failed. The message never carries details.

ForbiddenOrPolicyDeniedOrGuardrailBlocke.description: `FORBIDDEN`: The caller lacks the scope or the right this operation requires. `details.reason` is `two_factor_setup_required` where the instance requires two-factor sign-in and the person signed in with a password, or the owner of the personal key, has not set it up: every operation but `me.get` is refused until they have. `POLICY_DENIED`: The instance's policy does not allow this operation from here. `details.operation` names it. `details.reason` is `approval_unavailable` where the policy asks for another person's approval and the call cannot wait for one; `details.guardrailId` then names the guardrail that asked for it, where one did. It is `workflow_deleted` where a step of a run of a published Workflow needs the confirmation its publish gave, and the Workflow was deleted since. It is `approval_stale` where a call that waited can no longer be approved because what it is about changed or a newer call replaced it. It is `confirmation_required` where a subagent made a call that needs a person's confirmation or approval: a subagent never waits for one, and the agent that started it makes the call instead. `GUARDRAIL_BLOCKED`: A guardrail refused the call. `details.guardrailId` names it. `details.reason` is `check_unavailable` where a check could not answer, by an error or a timeout; `details.guardrailId` then names the event that was checked.

IdempotencyKeyReusedOrOperationInProgres.description: `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`: The `Idempotency-Key` was already used for another operation or another input. Send a new key. `OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS`: The first call with this `Idempotency-Key` has not ended, or it was interrupted and its outcome is not known (`details.interrupted` is `true`). `details.operationRunId` names its run. An interrupted call is never run again under its key: check what it changed, then send a new key. `OUTPUT_NOT_RETAINED`: The call with this `Idempotency-Key` completed, and its answer is not kept: it was too large, or it held a secret that is shown once. Read the result from what the call changed. A secret is not shown again.

OperationRunId.description: `Operation-Run-Id`: The id of the Operation Run that records this call. Set on every answer of a recorded call, a refusal and a failure included. Every changing call is recorded. A reading call is recorded when it is refused, when it fails, or when its operation records every call; an allowed read that is not recorded answers without this header.

Location.description: `Location`: Where the Operation Run of a call that waits for an approval is read.

IdempotentReplayed.description: `Idempotent-Replayed`: `true` when the answer is the recorded one of an earlier call with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

followUp.description: What happens when this conversation has an active run. `queue` sends the message as the next turn. `steer` hands it to the running turn at its next step when the run is the caller's own under the same credential and the message has no attachments, and queues it otherwise. Without this option, an active run still returns CONFLICT.
